Bootstrap flag rates of the asymptotic item-restscore test

Source: R/bootstrap_restscore.R
RMitemRestscoreBoot.Rd

Draws bootstrap samples of size samplesize from data, runs the asymptotic item-restscore test of iarm::item_restscore() in each, and reports how often each item is flagged as overfit or underfit. This describes how stable the asymptotic flags are across samples of a given size. It is not a calibrated test of item fit. For that, use RMitemRestscoreCutoff() with RMitemRestscore().

Usage

RMitemRestscoreBoot(
  data,
  iterations = 200,
  samplesize = 600,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  cutoff = 5,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  output = "kable"
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0.

iterations

Integer. Number of bootstrap samples. Default 200.

samplesize

Integer. Size of each bootstrap sample. Default 600. Must not exceed nrow(data).

parallel

Logical. Run the bootstrap in parallel via mirai when it is installed. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. When NULL, getOption("mc.cores") is used. If that is unset too, a warning is given and the bootstrap runs sequentially.

cutoff

Numeric. The kable shows only items flagged in more than cutoff percent of the samples. Default 5. Not used by the other outputs.

verbose

Logical. Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

output

Character. "kable" (default) for a knitr::kable() table, "dataframe" for the summary per item, or "raw" for one row per item and bootstrap sample (for custom plots).

Value

  • output = "kable": a knitr_kable table of the items flagged in more than cutoff percent of the samples, with the columns Item, Item-restscore result, % of iterations, Conditional MSQ infit and Relative item location. The caption gives the number of samples, the sample size and the number of complete cases.

  • output = "dataframe": a data.frame with one row per item and result ("overfit", "underfit", "no misfit"), with the columns Item, item_restscore, n, n_tested, percent, Infit_MSQ and Relative_location. percent is n out of n_tested, the samples in which the item could be tested, and NA when it never could.

  • output = "raw": a data.frame with one row per item and bootstrap sample, with the columns iteration, Item, item_restscore, diff and diff_abs. Note that diff is expected minus observed gamma, the opposite sign of Difference in RMitemRestscore(). Rows for an item that could not be tested in that sample have NA in item_restscore, diff and diff_abs.

Details

What the percentage means. Each sample is tested with the asymptotic test of iarm::item_restscore() with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, and an item is flagged when its adjusted p is below .05, as overfit or underfit by the sign of the difference. The result inherits that test's calibration at samplesize. With the Rasch model true, it flags too many items as overfit in small or mistargeted samples of dichotomous items, too few items of any kind in large polytomous samples, and too few underfitting items at every sample size (see RMitemRestscore() and https://pgmj.github.io/rasch_book/chapters/restscore-asymptotic-null.html). The percentage is therefore how often that test flags an item in samples of size samplesize, not the probability that the item misfits, and it changes with samplesize. A low underfit percentage is weak evidence of fit.

Model. The full sample is fitted by CML with psychotools::pcmodel() (a dichotomous item is a 2-category partial credit model). The conditional infit MSQ (iarm::out_infit(), on complete cases) and the relative item location (the mean of the item's CML thresholds minus the mean WLE person location) are computed once on the full sample and shown for context. Each bootstrap sample is refitted by CML.

Samples that fail. A sample in which the model cannot be fitted is left out, and the caption and the counts include only the samples that could be used. A polytomous item that is constant in a sample makes that sample fail. A dichotomous item that is constant, or a polytomous item with an empty middle category, cannot be tested in that sample. It is then left out of that item's percentages, the other items keep the sample, and the caption lists the items with fewer samples. When a constant dichotomous item is left out, the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment in that sample covers only the items tested there, since iarm drops the item before testing. An item with an empty lowest category is shifted to start at 0 by psychotools and is still tested.

Parallel processing needs the optional mirai package. The iarm package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

References

Kreiner, S. (2011). A Note on Item-Restscore Association in Rasch Models. Applied Psychological Measurement, 35(7), 557-561. doi:10.1177/0146621611410227

See also

RMitemRestscore() and RMitemRestscoreCutoff() for a calibrated test, RMitemInfit().

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE)) {
set.seed(42)
sim_data <- as.data.frame(
  matrix(sample(0:1, 400 * 8, replace = TRUE), nrow = 400, ncol = 8)
)
colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:8)

# Few iterations for a fast example. Use 100 or more in real analyses.
# Default kable output (only items flagged > cutoff%)
RMitemRestscoreBoot(sim_data, iterations = 50, samplesize = 300,
                parallel = FALSE, seed = 1)

# Per-item summary data.frame (all classifications, including "no misfit")
summary_df <- RMitemRestscoreBoot(sim_data, iterations = 50, samplesize = 300,
                              parallel = FALSE, seed = 1,
                              output = "dataframe")

# Per-iteration long data for custom plotting
raw_df <- RMitemRestscoreBoot(sim_data, iterations = 50, samplesize = 300,
                          parallel = FALSE, seed = 1, output = "raw")

# Distribution of (expected - observed) across iterations, per item
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(ggplot2)
  ggplot(raw_df, aes(x = Item, y = diff)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_violin(fill = "grey90", colour = NA) +
    geom_jitter(aes(colour = item_restscore, shape = item_restscore),
                width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("overfit"   = "#0072B2",
                                   "underfit"  = "#D55E00",
                                   "no misfit" = "grey60")) +
    labs(y = "Expected minus observed item-restscore gamma",
         colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}
}
